text:
after 2 years in Thailand we finally got around to booking an appointment for a dental. clean and check up. We chose this place because there were good reviews. Sadly for me it was a bad first dental experience in Thailand (and that was just for a clean!) and I will never come back. I was meant to take my kids back for an appointment but I requested to cancel because this was so unprofessional (and not kid friendly - see my last point). To be fair, it wasn’t all bad, so I’ll outline the positives and negatives to help anyone considering this place with your decision.

Positives:
1) The place looked professional and appeared to be hygienic and well cleaned.
2) The clean was not bad - the dentist only used the ultrasonic scaler to clean, he didn’t follow with hand scaling to get the last bits of calculus (as they usually do in Australian dental clinics).
3) The clean was efficient, only taking 15 minutes. Maybe a little too efficient? (I was literally in and out of the chair without any rapport building nor conversation about my
Dental concerns.
4) I requested “no flouride” for health reasons, which was listed as 400B on their price list. They honored that request, but still charged me the same amount as my husband, who had fluoride 🤷🏻‍♀️. They gave me a bottle of alcohol mouthwash in place of the flouride, so maybe I was charged 400B for a tiny bottle of mouthwash instead 🤣 🤷🏻‍♀️

Negatives
1)  Poor patient care - as a first time patient to this clinic I had hoped to talk to the dentist about some minor dental concerns, but the dentist (who spoke some English) didn’t even ask. He was only interested in getting me in the chair, do the clean, and get me out.

2) Upon sitting in the chair, they immediately put a cloth with a hole over my face, that completely obstructed my view. This cloth covered my whole face, leaving only my mouth open to getting worked on. I understand that it is for protecting your face from getting splashed on, but at least explain what you are about to do before you cover someone’s face unannounced. At one point during the clean, the cloth was pushed up my nose so much it obstructed my breathing. Luckily I’m not claustrophobic, but if I was, that would have been a terrifying experience (especially if coupled with dental fear).

3) The dentist spent the ENTIRE time while  cleaning my teeth chatting with his young lady assistant, discussing their social plans, and what they’re doing for Songkran. Meanwhile I was semi suffocating under this cloth on my face while he cleaned my very sensitive teeth with the supersonic jet. Not once during the clean did he pause to check if I was ok. I guess if you don’t see the face of your patient, you might just forget there’s a living, breathing person under there?

4) Once the clean was over, again, no check in to see how I was, or if I have any dental concerns. I was so put off by this point as there was obviously no interested in dental care of a patient, that I didn’t even bother raising with them that I had a sore tooth that was bothering me. Ill be raising that with a dentist when I get around to it, in another two years time 🤣

5) Even though we requested and paid for a check up, all we really got was a clean. There was no examination of our gum health, checking the last time we got a mouth x-ray. Maybe I’m comparing too much with Australian standard and expecting too much? I just thought this would be the basic level of care from a dentist.

6) this is not dental related, but relevant if you have kids… they have a TV in the waiting area that was playing music from YouTube. Their choice of music was Thai music that had explicit couple scenes, violence, and yes, you guess it, gay men making out 🤮 . Could not be more appropriate for children I guess 🤣 👀

Because I try so hard to make sure my kids have a positive dental experience, there is NO WAY I am taking my kids to this place. I will be looking around for another dentist for our family.

text:
Wasted time, money, and feelings.

The first visit was to consult an orthodontist because I felt my teeth were crooked. The doctor gave good advice and ordered X-rays (both large and small films) to determine if braces were necessary and also noted receding gums. The X-ray results showed minimal tartar buildup, and a simple scaling was sufficient. However, some front teeth might need grinding and a visit to a periodontist, and the upper right tooth was starting to decay. They told me to wait for the scaling. In total, I paid 1,200 baht for the X-rays.

While waiting for the scaling and filling, the staff mentioned the periodontist wouldn't be back in three days and asked if I wanted to do everything at once. I agreed and scheduled an appointment to save time.

I arrived at my appointment at 6:30 PM. The staff asked me to fill out a form with questions about my appointment, even though they had called me beforehand. Then, they seemed to be reviewing my appointment slip. They quoted prices for various services: scaling 800-1500 baht, fillings 200-300 baht per side, and drilling 200-300 baht. We agreed.

Then, they came back and asked the doctor to take an additional X-ray of the upper right tooth, even though we were still sitting at the counter and hadn't even been put on the chair yet. They also said they could only do one thing at a time and couldn't do everything. But we'd already had the X-ray! We were getting annoyed, and the staff started getting rude. So we said, "Then just do the scaling." They even made us wait!

In the end, we canceled the scaling and asked for the first X-ray film back. The staff suddenly softened and spoke nicely, but we wasted a lot of time and felt very disappointed. Goodbye.
